text: In Alex Agyei-Agyiri's $\textbf{Unexpected Joy at Dawn}$, the character $\textbf{Aaron}$ Tsuru is a scientist working on a project to use $\textbf{Ant Hill}$ soil for building materials.
explanation: Aaron represents the frustrated intellectual whose innovations are ignored by the government.

text: The literary device used to substitute a mild or vague expression for one thought to be offensive or harsh is a $\textbf{Euphemism}$.
explanation: Example: Saying someone 'passed away' instead of 'died'.

text: In Buchi Emecheta's $\textbf{Second Class Citizen}$, the people of Ibuza believe that Adah should not be educated because she is a girl and her family will not benefit from her $\textbf{Bride Price}$.
explanation: The traditional view was that educating a girl only benefited her future husband's family.

text: The poem '$\textbf{Piano and Drums}$' uses the $\textbf{Drums}$ to symbolize the $\textbf{Primal}$ and vigorous nature of African culture.
explanation: The 'mystic rhythm' of the drums contrasts with the complex 'concerto' of the piano.

text: In August Wilson's $\textbf{Fences}$, $\textbf{Lyons}$ is Troy's eldest son who refuses to work a labor job, preferring to pursue being a $\textbf{Musician}$.
explanation: Lyons often visits Troy on paydays to borrow money, causing friction.

text: The poem '$\textbf{Crossing the Bar}$' uses the metaphor of a $\textbf{Sandbar}$ to represent the boundary between $\textbf{Life}$ and $\textbf{Death}$.
explanation: Crossing this boundary implies leaving the harbor of life for the open ocean of the afterlife.

text: In John Osborne's $\textbf{Look Back in Anger}$, the play is set entirely in the Porter's one-room $\textbf{Attic}$ flat in the $\textbf{Midlands}$.
explanation: The claustrophobic setting reflects the trapped feelings of the characters.

text: In Wole Soyinka's $\textbf{The Lion and the Jewel}$, $\textbf{Sadiku}$ is the head wife of $\textbf{Baroka}$ who acts as a go-between in his wooing of Sidi.
explanation: She is initially tricked by Baroka's lie about his impotence but remains a key figure in the village hierarchy.

text: The main character in a literary work, often the hero or the one with whom the audience identifies, is the $\textbf{Protagonist}$.
explanation: The story revolves around the protagonist's journey.

text: In $\textbf{Invisible Man}$, the narrator joins a political organization called the $\textbf{Brotherhood}$, which claims to work for the equality of all people.
explanation: The group is an allegory for the Communist Party and other radical political groups of the era.

text: The poem '$\textbf{The School Boy}$' compares a child in school to a $\textbf{Bird}$ in a $\textbf{Cage}$, unable to sing or fly freely.
explanation: William Blake uses this imagery to criticize the restrictive nature of formal education.

text: In $\textbf{Wuthering Heights}$, the primary motivation for $\textbf{Heathcliff}$'s actions throughout the novel is $\textbf{Revenge}$ against those who mistreated him.
explanation: His love for Catherine twists into a desire to destroy the Earnshaw and Linton families.

text: A word that imitates the sound it represents (e.g., 'buzz', 'hiss') is an instance of $\textbf{Onomatopoeia}$.
explanation: It adds auditory imagery to the text.

text: In $\textbf{Second Class Citizen}$, Adah secures a good job at the $\textbf{North Finchley Library}$, which gives her a sense of worth and financial independence.
explanation: This job is a sanctuary for her, contrasting with the chaos of her home life.

text: A statement that seems self-contradictory but expresses a possible truth is a $\textbf{Paradox}$.
explanation: Example: 'The child is father of the man'.

text: In $\textbf{Fences}$, $\textbf{Rose}$ serves as a buffer between Troy and his son Cory, often trying to act as a $\textbf{Peacemaker}$.
explanation: Rose wants to keep the family together, often mediating the conflict until Troy's betrayal.

text: The turning point in a story, where the conflict reaches its highest intensity, is the $\textbf{Climax}$.
explanation: It is the moment of decisive action or realization.

text: In $\textbf{Unexpected Joy at Dawn}$, the title suggests that $\textbf{Hope}$ and happiness can emerge even after a long night of $\textbf{Suffering}$.
explanation: The 'dawn' represents a new beginning after the darkness of xenophobia and separation.

text: The author's attitude toward the subject or audience is referred to as the $\textbf{Tone}$.
explanation: Tone can be sarcastic, serious, humorous, etc.

text: The poem '$\textbf{A Government Driver on his Retirement}$' uses $\textbf{Situational Irony}$ when the driver survives years of service only to die in a crash while $\textbf{Celebrating}$.
explanation: He dies drunk driving home from his own retirement party.

text: In $\textbf{Look Back in Anger}$, the central theme involves the conflict between the $\textbf{Working Class}$ and the $\textbf{Establishment}$.
explanation: Jimmy Porter is the voice of working-class frustration against the upper-class status quo.

text: A figure of speech in which a part is used to represent the whole is $\textbf{Synecdoche}$.
explanation: Example: 'All hands on deck' (hands = sailors).

text: In $\textbf{Second Class Citizen}$, Francis burns Adah's manuscript, '$\textbf{The Bride Price}$', symbolizing his desire to crush her $\textbf{Creative}$ spirit.
explanation: He tells her that her family will never be writers, reinforcing his control.

text: The repetition of vowel sounds in nearby words is called $\textbf{Assonance}$.
explanation: Example: 'The rain in Spain'.

text: In $\textbf{Invisible Man}$, the narrator's $\textbf{Briefcase}$ becomes a symbol of his emotional and psychological $\textbf{Baggage}$.
explanation: He carries it everywhere, containing items from his past that define and haunt him.

text: The use of humor, irony, exaggeration, or ridicule to expose and criticize people's stupidity or vices is $\textbf{Satire}$.
explanation: Satire is often used for social or political commentary.

text: In $\textbf{Unexpected Joy at Dawn}$, Nii Tackie's Nigerian name acts as a curse in Ghana, marking him as an '$\textbf{Alien}$'.
explanation: During the Alien Compliance Order, his name alone is enough to put him in danger.

text: Poetry that does not follow a specific meter or rhyme scheme is called $\textbf{Free Verse}$.
explanation: It allows for greater freedom of expression.

text: In $\textbf{The Lion and the Jewel}$, Sidi's vanity is inflated when her images appear in a $\textbf{Magazine}$ brought by the Stranger.
explanation: She believes her fame makes her superior to the common villagers and even the Bale.

text: The central idea or message of a work of literature is the $\textbf{Theme}$.
explanation: Themes are universal concepts like love, war, or betrayal.

text: In $\textbf{Wuthering Heights}$, the ghost of $\textbf{Catherine}$ appears to Lockwood at the window, setting the tone for the novel's $\textbf{Haunting}$ past.
explanation: The ghost represents the unresolved passion and pain of the previous generation.

text: The use of objects, characters, or actions to represent abstract ideas is $\textbf{Symbolism}$.
explanation: Example: A red rose symbolizing love.

text: In $\textbf{Second Class Citizen}$, Francis blames his failure to pass his $\textbf{Accountancy}$ exams on Adah and her 'nagging', rather than his own laziness.
explanation: He refuses to work, claiming he needs to study, yet repeatedly fails.

text: Irony that occurs when the audience knows something the characters do not is $\textbf{Dramatic Irony}$.
explanation: This creates tension as the audience waits for the characters to discover the truth.

text: In $\textbf{Look Back in Anger}$, Alison loses her $\textbf{Baby}$ after leaving Jimmy, a tragedy that eventually brings them back together.
explanation: The loss of the child humbles Alison and allows Jimmy to see her suffering.

text: A brief reference to a person, event, or place, real or fictitious, or to a work of art is an $\textbf{Allusion}$.
explanation: It connects the text to the wider world of knowledge.

text: In $\textbf{Unexpected Joy at Dawn}$, the narrative explores the theme of $\textbf{Migration}$ and the challenges faced by immigrants in West Africa.
explanation: The movement of people between Ghana and Nigeria is the central dynamic of the plot.

text: The poem '$\textbf{The Panic of Growing Older}$' uses the metaphor of a $\textbf{Copybook}$ to describe how the years fill up one's life.
explanation: The pages are filled faster than expected, symbolizing the rapid passage of time.

text: In $\textbf{Fences}$, Gabriel has a $\textbf{Metal Plate}$ in his head due to a war injury, which affects his mental state.
explanation: This injury is the source of the disability money that Troy used to buy his house.

text: A narrative poem, originally meant to be sung, that tells a dramatic story is a $\textbf{Ballad}$.
explanation: Ballads often deal with folklore, love, or tragedy.
